objectives: Verify order, patient identity and the container, and refuse to start if anything does not match.
Describe time limits and tubing rules from the Circular.
Recognise and stop for suspected reactions and escalate.

items.text: Indications and thresholds for transfusion are prescriber decisions; this draft does not state thresholds per your unit's documentation standard.
Check the order, patient identity and container as local policy requires; do not start if anything does not match; do not use a product that looks abnormal and contact the transfusion service.

Do not add medicines or solutions to the tubing or run them through it at the same time, except 0.9% sodium chloride unless approved; never use lactated Ringer's or other calcium-containing solutions with citrate-containing components (Circular).

The US Circular gives a four-hour limit after entry into a container; verify the applicable component-specific time limit, storage and expiry with the local transfusion service. Do not interpret this as permission to use a product past its authorised limit.
Use a sterile clot filter as the Circular describes and local policy requires; warm blood only when clinically indicated with a cleared warming device.
Use aseptic technique, monitor the patient as policy requires, and stop the transfusion and inform the team at the first sign of a reaction.
Who may check, start and monitor transfusions is set by local policy and competence.
Administration sets, filters and warmers follow the unit's supplies and the manufacturer's instructions.
Observe the patient before, during and after transfusion at the frequency in local policy (NICE NG24 recommendation 1.13 on monitoring).

New symptoms during or around transfusion require assessment even when fever is absent or another diagnosis seems possible; monitor vital signs and distinguish a mild isolated rash from respiratory or circulatory compromise before any clinician-directed decision about treatment or product disposition.
Start rate, vital-sign timings and the step sequence follow the transfusion service's procedure; no graded source was read per your unit's documentation standard.
Monitor for fever, rigors, breathlessness, rash, hypotension, pain and changes in condition.

For a suspected acute transfusion reaction, stop the transfusion promptly, assess the patient and vital-sign trend, request urgent clinical review, re-check patient/product identification, and contact the transfusion service. Preserve the implicated component and set for investigation as directed by the blood bank; do not restart it on the nurse's own authority. For respiratory distress, shock or other severe features, activate emergency care immediately; do not assume all breathlessness represents fluid overload. Do not restart a component implicated in a serious reaction.

Maintain venous access for assessment using the separate/new administration set and compatible saline specified by local policy; do not flush remaining blood in the implicated transfusion tubing into the patient. Exact line management and samples follow institutional transfusion-reaction procedures.
Febrile, allergic, haemolytic and respiratory reactions and bacterial contamination are described in the Circular's side-effect sections.
Record product identifiers, checks, times, observations, reactions and actions per unit and transfusion-service standard.

checklist.text: Check the order, patient identity and container against each other as local policy requires.
Inspect the product; do not use it if it looks abnormal and contact the transfusion service.
Use aseptic technique and the filter and warmer required by policy.
Give nothing else through the transfusion tubing except what the Circular allows.
Confirm the component-specific time limit and expiry with the transfusion service and follow local administration policy.
Observe the patient at the frequency in local policy.

Stop a suspected reaction, assess airway, breathing and circulation, activate emergency help for severe features, and notify the clinician and transfusion service. Never independently restart the implicated component.
Maintain venous access using a new set per local protocol; do not push blood remaining in the implicated tubing into the patient; preserve the product and set for blood-bank review.
Record identifiers, times, observations and any reaction.
